newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ahmsa files steel dumping suits.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ahmsa files steel dumping suits.

text.p: Mexican steel giant Altos Hornos de Mexico (Ahmsa) said Tuesday it had filed steel dumping suits against product imported into Mexico from Russia and Ukraine.
Ahmsa said it presented formal charges to Mexico's Trade Ministry concerning dumping of product for cut-to-length steel plate cut coming from the two nations.

"Based on official information of imports of steel, the company (Ahmsa) registered 31,000 tonnes (of product) entering Mexico from those countries between May and December 1996, with a dumping level of 64 percent (below international prices)," Ahmsa said.
Ahmsa said the imported volume represented around nine percent of apparent national consumption of cut-to-length sheet steel in the reference period.
The Monclova-based company said that in its dumping suit it claimed national prices of the product were affected, impacting Mexican steel companies.
Ahmsa did not name companies involved in importing from Russia and Ukraine.
